总结此阶段工作  这里又找到一个明确瓶颈：mask_from_score 21.6ms，主要是 torch scatter + bool mask + uint64 转换。这个可以直接打掉。我现在加一个 C++/CUDA binding：输入 K2 topk indices，直接
  输出 stage1 K1 uint64 tile mask，避免 Python scatter。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• CUDA mask builder 已接到 pybind。现在重新编译本地 infllm_v2 扩展；如果这里编过，后面就能把 mask_from_score 从 21ms 压到接近 topk 本身。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 脚本已切到 fast CUDA mask builder。先做 binding smoke，再重跑 L9。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• fast mask builder 有效：mask_from_score 从 21.6ms 降到 4.0ms。当前两调用还是 46.4ms > 40.4ms，但如果能 split 掉第二次 K2 first pass，估算会到约 38ms/layer，有净收益。接下来
  我看 row_max/row_sum 能否低风险存取，决定是否直接做 split-stage1 原型。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 做 split 原型前先把跨层数字补齐：现在 fast mask 的两调用总成本、以及“如果 row stats split 成功”的 projected 成本都要看。这样能判断值不值得继续改底层 stage1 控制流。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 跨层 projection 说明：L0 不能用，L9+ 只有 1.03-1.09x/layer 的保守收益。为了找更高收益点，我继续扫 topk，看看 768 或 512 是否在 L9+ recall 可接受同时显著降 masked K1 时间。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 我现在把这个路径接成在线可开关原型，默认关闭：K2 stage1 score -> fast CUDA mask -> masked K1 stage1。虽然两调用不是最终形态，但它能让我们在 server 上快速测不同 topk/radius
  的真实 prefill 影响，并为后续 split 版本复用同一套 mask builder。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 在线原型代码已通过语法检查。现在用 capture 直接调用 compressed_attention 做离线 smoke：确认 env 关闭时仍等于原路径，env 开启时能跑出 topk，并量一下 Python 层端到端耗时。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 离线 smoke 暴露了一个关键 bug：masked K1 的 skipped tile 现在留成 0，max-pool/topk 会把这些 0 当候选，导致最终 topk recall 只有 30%。这必须修：有 K1 mask 时 P 输出初值要是
  -inf，不是 0，这样没算的 tile 不参与 topk。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 我改了 C++ 初始化逻辑：只有 masked K1 path 用 -inf 初始化 P；未 masked 的旧路径仍是 0/empty 行为。现在需要重编扩展并重跑 offline smoke。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 重编成功。现在重跑刚才的 compressed_attention smoke，看 -inf 初始化后最终 topk 是否恢复到 candidate 预期附近。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 定位到真正原因了：masked kernel 跳 block 时，gP 输出指针仍按连续 block -kBlockN 移动，导致选中的 tile 写到了错误列；-inf 初始化不是主因。我要把 stage1 第二段 K1 写出改成按
  当前 n_block 直接定位输出列。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 修正后的 8 层 tile 指标更保守：L0 明确不能用；L9 在 topk=1024,r=8 只有 99.77% tile recall，其它后层大多 99.84-99.96%。这说明 fused K2 仍有速度上限，但必须有 layer-specific
  策略和 fallback，不能把它当 exact。

  进 kernel，我会把它固化成脚本扫 8 层。

  tile mask 真实进入 masked K1 stage1 后的耗时。

• 离线 tile-score 原型已经跑通并测了 masked stage1：L9 top-M=320 时 mask 免费条件下 39.36ms -> 28.64ms，top-M=384 时 39.36ms -> 32.76ms。这说明它更容易写 kernel，但收益和
  recall 的取舍比 token-topk 更紧。

  stage1_k2_candidate_recall.py:217 和 prefill/experiment-log.md:537。
  3. 新增了更适合写 kernel 的 tile-score 原型：prefill/stage1_k2_tile_candidate_recall.py:1。它把 K2 probability evidence 聚合到 512 个 K1 tile，再选 top-M tiles，避免 8192-
  token 大 topk。

  - L9 是后层最难点。
  - L9 top-M 320: tile recall 99.78%，masked stage1 39.36ms -> 28.64ms。

  速度天花板会明显变小。文档已更新在 prefill/roadmap.md:182。

  accuracy 风险。

  值得。因此下一步不能做“先 denom 再重扫 K2”的复杂原型，必须想办法在第一遍 K2 pass 内维护候选，或者转向别的高收益点。

  这条路基本需要降级。

  max 和 exp/softmax 单调等价。我加 logit_groupmax_norm 来验证它是否和 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• L9 验证成立：raw-logit tile max 归一化后和 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致，bf16 raw-logit 存储也一致。这把 kernel 难度再降一档：first pass 只维护 tile 的 raw logit max，不需要
  对 tile accumulator 做 online rescale。跑全层确认。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 全层确认：logit_groupmax_norm 和 logit_groupmax_norm_bf16 都与 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致，0 mismatch。这是比上一版更好的实现切入点：shared 里存 bf16 raw logit max，最后用
  已有 row max/sum 归一化。

  输出 stage1 K1 uint64 tile mask，避免 Python scatter。

  我看 row_max/row_sum 能否低风险存取，决定是否直接做 split-stage1 原型。

• raw K2 logits topk 不成立：真正有用的是“16 个 group 的 normalized prob sum”，raw sum/max recall 掉得很厉害。也就是说单 kernel 内若想保留现有 K2 candidate 质量，不能只在第一
  段 masked logits 上随手做 topk，至少要拿到 K2 denom 后的 prob-sum 信息。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 我发现一个验证脚本层面的坑：stage1_k2_candidate_recall.py 一次扫多个 topk 时先取最大 topk 且 sorted=False，再切前缀会让较小 topk 的 recall 失真。单个 topk 的旧结论不受影
  响，但多 topk 表需要修正；我先修脚本再重扫。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 我把 recall 脚本补成 tile 级指标，因为实际 K1 mask 跳过的是 64-token tile，不是单个 sparse block。这样能直接回答“candidate mask 已经有了时，能跳过多少 K1 tile、漏多少 exact
  topk tile”。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 修正后的 8 层 tile 指标更保守：L0 明确不能用；L9 在 topk=1024,r=8 只有 99.77% tile recall，其它后层大多 99.84-99.96%。这说明 fused K2 仍有速度上限，但必须有 layer-specific
  策略和 fallback，不能把它当 exact。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 当前没有后台长跑任务。prefill/ 目录仍是未跟踪实验目录，所以 git diff 不显示这些文档/脚本改动；我继续把这次修正后的结论写进 prefill/experiment-log.md 和 roadmap.md，方便后续
  复现。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 下一步我不再只看 K2 token topk，而是验证更适合内核实现的 tile-score 方案：K2 prob-sum 先聚合/扩张到 512 个 K1 tile，再选 top-M tiles。这样内核里只需要对 512 个 tile 排名，
  而不是对 8192 个 K2 token 做大 topk。

• tile-score 方案初测有价值：L9 上 top-M=320 个 tile 时 recall 接近 K2 token topk1024/r8，候选比例 62.5%；top-M=280 更快但 recall 降一点。这个形态比 8192-token topk 更适合写
  进 kernel，我会把它固化成脚本扫 8 层。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• tile-score 多层结果：L0 仍失败；L9 是后层里最难的。top-M=320 的候选比例固定 62.5%，L9 tile recall 99.78%；top-M=384 候选 75%，L9 99.92%、其它后层约 99.98%+。我现在测这些
  tile mask 真实进入 masked K1 stage1 后的耗时。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 离线 tile-score 原型已经跑通并测了 masked stage1：L9 top-M=320 时 mask 免费条件下 39.36ms -> 28.64ms，top-M=384 时 39.36ms -> 32.76ms。这说明它更容易写 kernel，但收益和
  recall 的取舍比 token-topk 更紧。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  1. exact stage1 -> blockmax/topk 分支已经验证：结果 exact，但性能不可用。L9 capture 上旧路径约 42.6ms，blockmax fused 约 188.8ms，原因是把 pooling 放进 stage1 会破坏原
  kernel 的吞吐。记录在 prefill/experiment-log.md:468。
  2. 修正了 K2 recall 脚本的多 topk bug，并补了 tile 级指标。真实可用指标应看 tile recall，因为 K1 mask 跳过的是 64-token tile。记录在 prefill/
  stage1_k2_candidate_recall.py:217 和 prefill/experiment-log.md:537。
  3. 新增了更适合写 kernel 的 tile-score 原型：prefill/stage1_k2_tile_candidate_recall.py:1。它把 K2 probability evidence 聚合到 512 个 K1 tile，再选 top-M tiles，避免 8192-
  token 大 topk。

  关键结果：

  - L0 仍必须 exact。
  - L9 是后层最难点。
  - L9 top-M 320: tile recall 99.78%，masked stage1 39.36ms -> 28.64ms。
  - L9 top-M 384: tile recall 99.92%，masked stage1 39.36ms -> 32.76ms。
  - 后层 top-M 320 大约 99.78-99.97% tile recall；top-M 384 大约 99.88-99.99%。

  当前最高收益实现方向更新为：单 kernel 内做 K2 probability tile-score top-M candidate，L0 exact，L9+ selective K1。这比 K2 token topk 更可实现，但如果必须用 top-M 384 才稳，
  速度天花板会明显变小。文档已更新在 prefill/roadmap.md:182。

  验证已跑：两个新/修改脚本都 py_compile 通过；当前没有后台 server 或长跑任务。

  top-M384 32.65ms。

  - 文档更新：prefill/experiment-log.md:605、prefill/roadmap.md:182

  top-M 原型，但收益窗口已经比较窄：top-M 320 有速度，recall 偏险；top-M 384 更稳，但只剩约 6-7ms/layer 的 mask-free 空间。

  accuracy 风险。

• 一个重要收益模型出来了：如果 in-kernel tile-score 需要额外重扫 K2，一层要再花约 first-pass 8.4ms，top-M320 的尾段净收益会从 75ms/chunk 掉到大约 16ms/chunk，top-M384 基本不
  值得。因此下一步不能做“先 denom 再重扫 K2”的复杂原型，必须想办法在第一遍 K2 pass 内维护候选，或者转向别的高收益点。

  这条路基本需要降级。

  tile 累积并处理 online rescale，要么额外扫一次 K2。额外 K2 扫大概率吃掉收益，所以我下一步先重新量化“便宜 one-pass evidence”在所有 captured 层上的 recall，看看是否有足够精度

      - top-M352 99.956% / 99.870%
      - top-M384 99.978% / 99.916%
      - 相比 fp32 online，每层 hit diff 只有 [-2, +6] 量级

  这让 CUDA 方案更现实：现有 stage1 smem 约 36KB/CTA，fp32 tile max 要额外 32KB，总 68KB；bf16 tile max 只要额外 16KB，总约 52KB/CTA，更适合先做 kernel prototype。

  我写了实现设计文档：prefill/stage1-groupmax-design.md:52。当前首选路线是 one-kernel fused stage1：

  1. K2 first pass 内维护 bf16 per-group tile max
  2. row max/sum 仍用 fp32
  3. row sum finalize 后归一化并 sum 16 group rows
  4. 本 CTA 内 top-M 生成 local 512-bit mask
  验证：相关脚本 py_compile 通过；当前没有 server/bench 残留进程。下一步就是动 CUDA：先做 bf16 tile-max + local mask 的 stage1 kernel prototype。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 发现一个更关键的简化：prob_groupmax_sum 不需要在线 rescale tile max。本质上每个 group/tile 只要保留 raw logit max，最后用 first pass 已有的 row max/sum 做一次归一化即可；
  max 和 exp/softmax 单调等价。我加 logit_groupmax_norm 来验证它是否和 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• L9 验证成立：raw-logit tile max 归一化后和 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致，bf16 raw-logit 存储也一致。这把 kernel 难度再降一档：first pass 只维护 tile 的 raw logit max，不需要
  对 tile accumulator 做 online rescale。跑全层确认。

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

• 全层确认：logit_groupmax_norm 和 logit_groupmax_norm_bf16 都与 prob_groupmax_sum 完全一致，0 mismatch。这是比上一版更好的实现切入点：shared 里存 bf16 raw logit max，最后用
  已有 row max/sum 归一化。

54	__forceinline__ __device__ void hdim16_reduce(

62	    auto tensor = make_tensor(acc_S.data(), flash::convert_layout_acc_rowcol(acc_S.layout()));
63	    const int warp_id = threadIdx.x / 32;
64	    const int lane_id = threadIdx.x % 32;

66	    // const int row_idx_offset = row_idx_offset_ + warp_id * 16 + lane_id / 4;
67	    const int col_idx_offset = 0 + (lane_id % 4) * 2;
68	    const int row_idx_offset = 0 + warp_id * 16 + lane_id / 4;
69	
70	    // step 1: 线程内部求和 (v0 + v2)
71	    using TensorT = decltype(make_tensor<float>(Shape< Int<size<0, 1>(tensor)>, Int<size<1>(tensor)> >{}));
72	    TensorT v02;
73	    clear(v02);
74	    #pragma unroll
75	    for (int mi = 0; mi < size<0, 1>(tensor); ++mi) {
76	        #pragma unroll
77	        for (int nj = 0; nj < size<1, 1>(tensor); ++nj) {

80	                const int col_idx_v02 = j * size<1, 1>(tensor) + nj;
81	                const float v0 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(0, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
82	                const float v2 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(1, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
83	                v02(mi, col_idx_v02) = v0 + v2;
84	            }
85	        }
86	    }
87	
88	    // step 2: warp 内部蝶形求和
89	    SumOp<float> sum_op;
90	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<16>(v02, sum_op);
91	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<8> (v02, sum_op);
92	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<4> (v02, sum_op);
93	
94	    // step 3: copy 到 global mem
95	    cutlass::NumericConverter<Element, float> converter;
96	    if (lane_id < 4) {
97	        #pragma unroll
98	        for (int mi = 0; mi < size<0, 1>(tensor); ++mi) {
99	            const int row_idx_base = row_idx_offset + mi * warp_row_stride;
100	            #pragma unroll

102	                const int col_idx_base = col_idx_offset + nj * 8;

107	                    g_Sh(row_idx_base/16, col_idx) = converter(v02(mi, col_idx_v02)); // ignore /16 since it's too slow
108	                }
109	            }

139	    (void)row_idx_offset_;
140	    (void)warp_row_stride;
141

143	
144	    using TensorT = decltype(make_tensor<float>(Shape< Int<size<0, 1>(tensor)>, Int<size<1>(tensor)> >{}));
145	    TensorT v02;

147	    #pragma unroll

153	                const int col_idx_v02 = j * size<1, 1>(tensor) + nj;
154	                const float v0 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(0, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
155	                const float v2 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(1, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
156	                v02(mi, col_idx_v02) = v0 + v2;
157	            }
158	        }
159	    }
160	
161	    SumOp<float> sum_op;
162	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<16>(v02, sum_op);
163	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<8> (v02, sum_op);
164	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<4> (v02, sum_op);
165	
166	    cutlass::NumericConverter<Element, float> converter;
167	    if (lane_id < 4) {
168	        #pragma unroll
169	        for (int mi = 0; mi < size<0, 1>(tensor); ++mi) {
170	            #pragma unroll
171	            for (int nj = 0; nj < size<1, 1>(tensor); ++nj) {
172	                const int col_idx_base = col_idx_offset + nj * 8;
173	                #pragma unroll
174	                for (int j = 0; j < size<1, 0>(tensor); ++j) {
175	                    const int col_idx = col_idx_base + j;
176	                    const int col_idx_v02 = j * size<1, 1>(tensor) + nj;
177	                    Element v = converter(v02(mi, col_idx_v02));

189	        if (pool_idx < out_stride) {
190	            uint16_t max_bits = 0;
191	            const int score_idx0 = local_pool * 4 - 1;
192	            if (score_idx0 >= 0) {
193	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[score_idx0]);
194	            }
195	            if (local_pool < 16) {
196	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4]);
197	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 1]);
198	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 2]);
199	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 3]);
200	            }
201	            if (local_pool == 0 || local_pool == 16) {
202	                const uint16_t old_bits = element_to_u16(row[pool_idx]);
203	                max_bits = max(max_bits, old_bits);
204	                row[pool_idx] = u16_to_element<Element>(max_bits);
205	            } else {
206	                row[pool_idx] = u16_to_element<Element>(max_bits);
207	            }
208	        }
209	    }

215	__forceinline__ __device__ auto get_lse_tile(const Params &params, const int bidb, const int bidh, const int m_block, const BlockInfo</*Varlen=*/!Is_even_MN> &binfo) {
216	        // When params.unpadded_lse is false, LSE is written as (b, h, seqlen_q) - this is non-variable seqlen path.
217	        // Otherwise, when params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped is true, it is written as (h, seqlen_q, b) to account for seqlen_q <-> h swapping trick.
218	        // Otherwise, it's written as (h, b, seqlen_q).
219	        const bool varlen_q = params.unpadded_lse && !params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped;
220	        auto lse_offset = varlen_q ? binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb) : 0;
221	        auto gmem_ptr_lse = make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementAccum*>(params.softmax_lse_ptr) + lse_offset);
222	
223	        auto lse_shape = varlen_q ? make_shape(1, params.h, params.total_q) : make_shape(params.b, params.h, params.seqlen_q);
224	        auto lse_stride = params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped ? make_stride(1, params.seqlen_q * params.b, params.b) : (
225	            params.unpadded_lse ? make_stride(params.h * params.total_q, params.total_q, 1) :  make_stride(params.h * params.seqlen_q, params.seqlen_q, 1)
226	            );
227	
228	        auto lse_layout = make_layout(lse_shape, lse_stride);
229	        Tensor mLSE = make_tensor(gmem_ptr_lse, lse_layout);
230	        auto mLSE_slice = varlen_q ? mLSE(0, bidh, _) : mLSE(bidb, bidh, _);
231	        return local_tile(mLSE_slice, Shape<Int<kBlockM>>{}, make_coord(m_block));
232	}

更现实的方向：先看 stage1 各段实际耗时分布（K2 first pass / K1 second pass / writeout），定位最大的可优化点。

243	def _derive_sparse_cache_seqlens_from_topk(
244	    topk_idx: torch.Tensor,
245	    token_to_bs: torch.Tensor,
246	    token_pos_in_bs: torch.Tensor,
247	    seqlen_k_sparse_bs: torch.Tensor,
248	    block_size: int,
249	    dtype: torch.dtype,
250	) -> torch.Tensor:
251	    # Mirrors get_block_table_v2 causal truncation without scanning sparse_page_table.
252	    limit = torch.minimum(
253	        seqlen_k_sparse_bs[token_to_bs],
254	        token_pos_in_bs,
255	    ).view(1, -1, 1)
256	    block_starts = topk_idx * block_size
257	    valid_lens = (limit - block_starts).clamp_(min=0, max=block_size)
258	    valid_lens.masked_fill_(topk_idx < 0, 0)
259	    return valid_lens.sum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.int32).transpose(0, 1).reshape(-1).to(dtype=dtype)
260	
261	
262	def _get_block_page64_offset(
263	    page_table: torch.Tensor,
264	    seq_lens_cpu,
265	    block_size: int,
266	) -> int:
267	    """Return a common physical token offset for 64-token page views, or -1.
268	
269	    The page64 sparse stage2 path is exact only when every logical 64-token
270	    block maps to a physically contiguous block with the same modulo offset.
271	    Token allocator page_size=1 usually satisfies this for chunked prefill, but
272	    prefix reuse or fragmentation can break it, so this guard is required.
273	    """
274	    if page_table.numel() == 0:
275	        return -1
276	    max_len = max(int(x) for x in seq_lens_cpu)
277	    if max_len <= 0:
278	        return -1
279	    starts_pos = torch.arange(0, max_len, block_size, device=page_table.device)
280	    starts = page_table[:, starts_pos]
281	    lens = torch.as_tensor(seq_lens_cpu, dtype=torch.long, device=page_table.device)
282	    start_mask = starts_pos.view(1, -1) < lens.view(-1, 1)
283	    if not bool(start_mask.any().item()):
284	        return -1
285	
286	    offsets = starts[start_mask] % block_size
287	    first_offset = int(offsets[0].item())
288	    if not bool((offsets == first_offset).all().item()):
289	        return -1
290	
291	    full_mask = (starts_pos + block_size - 1).view(1, -1) < lens.view(-1, 1)
292	    if bool(full_mask.any().item()):
293	        full_cols = starts_pos[starts_pos + block_size - 1 < page_table.shape[1]]
294	        ends = page_table[:, full_cols + block_size - 1]
295	        starts_full = page_table[:, full_cols]
296	        full_mask = (full_cols + block_size - 1).view(1, -1) < lens.view(-1, 1)
297	        if not bool((ends[full_mask] == starts_full[full_mask] + block_size - 1).all().item()):
298	            return -1
299	    return first_offset

54	    return (

62	def forced_block_mask(
63	    *,
64	    row_ids: torch.Tensor,
65	    cache_len: int,
66	    block_count: int,
67	    block_size: int,
68	    init_blocks: int,
69	    local_blocks: int,
70	    device: torch.device,
71	) -> torch.Tensor:
72	    block_ids = torch.arange(block_count, device=device)
73	    q_blocks = (row_ids.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64) + cache_len) // block_size
74	    init_mask = block_ids.view(1, -1) < init_blocks
75	    local_start = torch.clamp(q_blocks - local_blocks, min=0)
76	    local_end = torch.clamp(q_blocks, max=block_count - 1)
77	    local_mask = (block_ids.view(1, -1) >= local_start.view(-1, 1)) & (
78	        block_ids.view(1, -1) <= local_end.view(-1, 1)
79	    )
80	    return init_mask | local_mask

93	    device: torch.device,
94	) -> torch.Tensor:
95	    q_rows = q_rows.to(device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
96	    k2 = k2[:actual_k2_len].to(device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
97	    q_len, q_heads, head_dim = q_rows.shape
98	    kv_heads = k2.shape[1]
99	    group = q_heads // kv_heads
100	
101	    q_grouped = q_rows.reshape(q_len, kv_heads, group, head_dim).permute(1, 2, 0, 3).contiguous()
102	    k2_t = k2.permute(1, 2, 0).contiguous()
103	    logits = torch.matmul(q_grouped, k2_t.unsqueeze(1)).mul_(head_dim ** -0.5).float()
104	
105	    k2_ids = torch.arange(actual_k2_len, device=device)
106	    q_blocks = (row_ids.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64) + cache_len) // block_size
107	    valid = k2_ids.view(1, 1, 1, -1) <= q_blocks.view(1, 1, -1, 1)
108	    valid &= ~forced_sparse[:, :actual_k2_len].view(1, 1, q_len, actual_k2_len)
109	    logits.masked_fill_(~valid, float("-inf"))
110	
111	    probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
112	    score = probs.sum(dim=1)
113	    return score.topk(min(topk, actual_k2_len), dim=-1, sorted=False).indices

m_block_dim = 1 for production stage1_k1_mask\nprint(f\"seqlen_k_rounded={seqlen_k_rounded}, num_blocks_n={num_blocks_n}, uint64_per_row={uint64_per_row}, total_q_div_m_block={total_q_div_m_block}\")\n\ndef make_blockmask(keep_ratio):\n    \"\"\"Build a uint64 blockmask where keep_ratio fraction of tiles are 1.\"\"\"\n    num_keep = int(num_blocks_n * keep_ratio)\n    if num_keep == 0:\n        num_keep = 1\n    # max_k1 = int(d[\"max_seqlen_k1\"])\ncache_len = int(d[\"cache_lens\"][0].item())\nblock_size = int(d[\"block_size\"]); kernel_stride = int(d[\"kernel_stride\"])\nsparse_topk = int(d[\"sparse_topk\"]); init_blocks = int(d[\"init_blocks\"]); local_blocks = int(d[\"local_blocks\"])\nexact_topk = d[\"exact_topk_idx\"].cuda().to(torch.int64)\ntotal_q, q_heads, head_dim = q_raw.shape\nkv_heads = k1.shape[1]; group = q_heads // kv_heads\nq_adj = (q_raw.reshape(total_q, kv_heads, group, head_dim).transpose(1,2).reshape(total_q*group, kv_heads, head_dim).contiguous())\ncu_q_adj = (cu_q.to(torch.int64) * group).to(torch.int32); max_q_adj = max_q * group\n\nseqlen_k_rounded = ((max_k1 + 127) // 128) * 128\nnum_blocks_n = seqlen_k_rounded // 64\nuint64_per_row = (num_blocks_n + 63) // 64\nsparse_blocks_per_tile = block_size // kernel_stride * 4  # 16: each K1 tile contains 16 sparse blocks\n# Actually: max_pooling output length = seqlen_k1 / (kernel_stride*kernel_stride/block_size) hmm.\n# Let's just check: exact_topk max ~8190, so num_sparse_blocks ~= 8192 = num_blocks_n * 16\n# So sparse_block_idx // 16 = K1_tile_idx\nprint(f\"num_K1_tiles={num_blocks_n}, exact_topk max={exact_topk.max().item()}, sparse/K1_tile = {(exact_topk.max().item()+1)/num_blocks_n}\")\n\ndef derive_topk(score):\n    bs = max_pooling_1d_varlen(\n        score.contiguous(), cu_q, cu_k1, d[\"cache_lens\"].cuda().to(torch.int32),\n        max_q, max_k1,\n        local_blocks=local_blocks, init_blocks=init_blocks,\n        block_size=block_size, stride=kernel_stride, total_q=-1)\n    return bs.topk(min(sparse_topk, bs.shape[-1]), dim=-1, sorted=True).indices.sort(-1).values.to(torch.int32), bs\n\ndef build_mask_from_k1_tile_set(k1_tiles_per_row):\n    \"\"\"k1_tiles_per_row is bool tensor (kv_heads, total_q, num_blocks_n).\"\"\"\n    bits = torch.zeros((kv_heads, total_q, uint64_per_row), dtype=torch.int64, device=\"cuda\")\n    for b in range(num_blocks_n):\n        u = b // 64; bp = b % 64\n        bits[..., u] |= (k1_tiles_per_row[..., b].long() << bp)\n    return bits.contiguous()\n\ndef build_ideal_mask(k1_radius=0):\n    \"\"\"Convert exact_topk sparse_block_idx -> K1 tile idx, plus radius (in K1 tile units).\"\"\"\n    k1_tile_from_exact = exact_topk // 16  # sparse_block -> K1 tile\n    mask_bool = torch.zeros((kv_heads, total_q, num_blocks_n), dtype=torch.bool, device=\"cuda\")\n    for r in range(-k1_radius, k1_radius + 1):\n        tile_ids = (k1_tile_from_exact + r).clamp(min=0, max=num_blocks_n - 1)\n        mask_bool.scatter_(2, tile_ids, True)\n    # Force init/local\n    row_ids = torch.arange(total_q, device=\"cuda\")\n    q_blocks = ((row_ids + cache_len) // block_size).long()\n    block_ids = torch.arange(num_blocks_n, device=\"cuda\")\n    init_m = block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) < init_blocks\n    local_start = (q_blocks - local_blocks).clamp(min=0).view(1, -1, 1)\n    local_end = q_blocks.clamp(max=num_blocks_n - 1).view(1, -1, 1)\n    local_m = (block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) >= local_start) & (block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) <= local_end)\n    mask_bool |= init_m.expand_as(mask_bool) | local_m.expand_as(mask_bool)\n    keep = mask_bool.sum(dim=-1).float()\n    print(f\"  k1_radius={k1_radius}: keep mean/max/min = {keep.mean().item():.1f}/{keep.max().item()}/{keep.min().item()}\")\n    return build_mask_from_k1_tile_set(mask_bool)\n\ndef bench(fn, iters=20, warmup=3):\n    torch.cuda.synchronize()\n    for _ in range(warmup): out = fn()\n    torch.cuda.synchronize()\n    times = []\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        s = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True); e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)\n        s.record(); out = fn(); e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()\n        times.append(s.elapsed_time(e))\n    return sum(times)/len(times), out\n\ndef run_baseline():\n    return infllmv2_attn_stage1(q_adj, k1, k2,\n        cu_seqlens_q=cu_q_adj, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k1, cu_seqlens_v=cu_k2,\n        max_seqlen_q=max_q_adj, max_seqlen_k=max_k1, causal=True)\n\ndef run_masked(mask):\n    return infllm_v2_C.varlen_fwd_stage1_k1_mask(\n        q_adj, k1, k2, None, cu_q_adj, cu_k1, cu_k2, None, None, None, None,\n        max_q_adj, max_k1, 0.0, head_dim ** -0.5, False, True, -1, -1, 0.0, True, None, mask)[0]\n\nt_base, score_base = bench(run_baseline)\ntopk_base, bs_base = derive_topk(score_base)\nmatch_base = (topk_base.long() == exact_topk).all().item()\ndiff_base = int((topk_base.long() != exact_topk).sum().item())\nprint(f\"\\nbaseline stage1: {t_base:.3f} ms  topk_match_exact={match_base}  diff={diff_base}\")\nprint(f\"score_base.shape={tuple(score_base.shape)} block_score.shape={tuple(bs_base.shape)}\")\n\nprint(f\"\\n=== Ideal K1 mask ceiling (K1 tile units) ===\")\nfor r in [0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16]:\n    mask = build_ideal_mask(r)\n    t, score = bench(lambda: run_masked(mask))\n    topk_new, bs_new = derive_topk(score)\n    same_as_base = (topk_new.long() == topk_base.long()).all().item()\n    diff_base_topk = int((topk_new.long() != topk_base.long()).sum().item())\n    diff_exact = int((topk_new.long() != exact_topk).sum().item())\n    keep_count = ((torch.tensor(1, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.int64) << torch.arange(64, device=\"cuda\")) &\n                  mask.unsqueeze(-1)).bool().sum(dim=(-1, -2)).float().mean().item()\n    print(f\"  k1_radius={r}: time={t:.3f} ms  diff_vs_base={diff_base_topk}  diff_vs_exact={diff_exact}\")\nPY\npython3 /tmp/bench_k1_mask_ideal2.py",
  "description": "K1 mask ceiling with correct K1-tile unit conversion"
}

reshape to (total_q, 2, 16, 128)\n    q_rs = q_adj.reshape(total_q, group, kv_heads, head_dim).transpose(1, 2)  # (total_q, kv_heads, group, head_dim)\n    k2_view = k2[:actual_k2_len]  # (actual_k2_len, kv_heads, head_dim)\n    # logits (kv_heads, group, total_q, actual_k2_len) = (q_rs[..., :head_dim] @ k2_view.T)\n    # Use Q (total_q, kv_heads, group, head_dim) -> permute to (kv_heads, group, total_q, head_dim)\n    Q = q_rs.permute(1, 2, 0, 3).contiguous()  # (kv_heads, group, total_q, head_dim)\n    K = k2_view.permute(1, 2, 0).contiguous()  # (kv_heads, head_dim, actual_k2_len)\n    logits = (Q @ K.unsqueeze(1)).float() * (head_dim ** -0.5)  # (kv_heads, group, total_q, actual_k2_len)\n    \n    # Causal mask: K2 token i valid for query at position q if i <= (q+cache_len)/block_size\n    k2_ids = torch.arange(actual_k2_len, device=\"cuda\")\n    q_blocks = (torch.arange(total_q, device=\"cuda\") + cache_len) // block_size\n    valid = k2_ids.view(1, 1, 1, -1) <= q_blocks.view(1, 1, -1, 1)\n    logits.masked_fill_(~valid, float(\"-inf\"))\n    \n    # prob_groupmax_sum: per K1 tile, take max over K2 columns mapping to that tile (with radius=0), then sum over group\n    # K2 token -> K1 tile: k2_id // 16 (since 16 sparse blocks per K1 tile, K2 stride == sparse block stride)\n    # Actually: K2 token corresponds to ... let me think. compressed K2 = K1 stride 16, so 1 K2 token covers 16 K1 tokens.\n    # K1 tile = 64 K1 tokens = 4 K2 tokens. So K2 token / 4 = K1 tile idx (compressed kBlockN axis).\n    # But in stage1, kBlockN=64 means 64 K2 cols per stage1 tile, which corresponds to 4 K1 tiles. \n    # Wait there's no fixed \"K1 tile\" in K2 space. Let me re-examine the evidence aggregation.\n    # \n    # The mask is on K1 axis tiles (kBlockN=64 K1 cols). 1 K1 tile = 64 K1 tokens.\n    # K2 token = 16 K1 tokens (since K2 stride=16). So 1 K1 tile = 64/16 = 4 K2 tokens.\n    # K2_token_idx // 4 = K1_tile_idx\n    k2_to_k1tile = k2_ids // 4  # (actual_k2_len,) values in [0, actual_k2_len/4)\n    max_tile = int(k2_to_k1tile.max().item()) + 1\n    if max_tile > num_blocks_n:\n        max_tile = num_blocks_n\n    \n    # Softmax normalize K2 logits per (kv_heads, group, row)\n    probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)  # (kv_heads, group, total_q, actual_k2_len)\n    \n    # prob_groupmax: for each (kv_heads, group, row, K1_tile), take max over K2 tokens in that tile\n    group_tile_max = torch.full((kv_heads, group, total_q, num_blocks_n), -float(\"inf\"), device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.float32)\n    group_tile_max.scatter_reduce_(3, k2_to_k1tile.view(1, 1, 1, -1).expand_as(probs), probs, reduce=\"amax\", include_self=True)\n    \n    # Sum over group=16\n    tile_score = group_tile_max.where(torch.isfinite(group_tile_max), torch.zeros_like(group_tile_max)).sum(dim=1)  # (kv_heads, total_q, num_blocks_n)\n    \n    # Force init/local blocks to +inf so they're always kept\n    row_ids = torch.arange(total_q, device=\"cuda\")\n    q_blocks_real = (row_ids + cache_len) // block_size\n    block_ids = torch.arange(num_blocks_n, device=\"cuda\")\n    init_m = block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) < init_blocks\n    local_start = (q_blocks_real - local_blocks).clamp(min=0).view(1, -1, 1)\n    local_end = q_blocks_real.clamp(max=num_blocks_n - 1).view(1, -1, 1)\n    local_m = (block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) >= local_start) & (block_ids.view(1, 1, -1) <= local_end)\n    forced = init_m.expand_as(tile_score) | local_m.expand_as(tile_score)\n    tile_score = tile_score.masked_fill(forced, float(\"inf\"))\n dtype=torch.bool)\n    mask_bool.scatter_(2, top_idx, True)\n    return mask_bool\n\ndef bench(fn, iters=20, warmup=3):\n    torch.cuda.synchronize()\n    for _ in range(warmup): out = fn()\n    torch.cuda.synchronize()\n    times = []\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        s = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True); e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)\n        s.record(); out = fn(); e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize()\n        times.append(s.elapsed_time(e))\n    return sum(times)/len(times), out\n\ndef run_baseline():\n    return infllmv2_attn_stage1(q_adj, k1, k2,\n        cu_seqlens_q=cu_q_adj, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k1, cu_seqlens_v=cu_k2,\n        max_seqlen_q=max_q_adj, max_seqlen_k=max_k1, causal=True)\n\ndef run_masked(mask):\n    return infllm_v2_C.varlen_fwd_stage1_k1_mask(\n        q_adj, k1, k2, None, cu_q_adj, cu_k1, cu_k2, None, None, None, None,\n        max_q_adj, max_k1, 0.0, head_dim ** -0.5, False, True, -1, -1, 0.0, True, None, mask)[0]\n\nt_base, score_base = bench(run_baseline)\ntopk_base, bs_base = derive_topk(score_base)\nprint(f\"baseline stage1: {t_base:.3f} ms\")\n\nprint(\"\\n=== K2-evidence-derived K1 mask vs baseline topk ===\")\nfor top_m in [320, 256, 192, 128, 96, 64, 48, 32]:\n    mask_bool = k2_evidence_to_k1_mask(top_m)\n    keep = mask_bool.sum(dim=-1).float()\n    mask = build_mask_from_bool(mask_bool)\n    t, score = bench(lambda: run_masked(mask))\n    topk_new, bs_new = derive_topk(score)\n    diff_base = int((topk_new.long() != topk_base.long()).sum().item())\n    rec_vs_base = 1.0 - diff_base / (kv_heads * total_q * sparse_topk)\n    print(f\"  top_M={top_m:4d}: keep mean={keep.mean().item():.1f} max={keep.max().item():.0f}  time={t:6.3f} ms  diff_vs_base={diff_base:>7d}  approx_recall={rec_vs_base*100:.3f}%\")\nPY\npython3 /tmp/bench_k2_evidence_mask.py 2>&1 | head -50",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /user_4813494d/openbmb

# No-spec target server for Marlin/b12x dispatch validation.
# Keep this separate from start_eagle.sh so e2e speed runs cannot
# accidentally include speculative decoding.
TARGET_MODEL="${EAGLE_TARGET_MODEL:-/user_4813494d/models/openbmb/MiniCPM-SALA-gptq46-calib90-90k-NVFP4}"
PORT="${SGLANG_PORT:-30000}"

SGLANG_MINICPM_PLAN_CACHE="${SGLANG_MINICPM_PLAN_CACHE:-1}" \
SGLANG_FP4_TUNE_CACHE="${SGLANG_FP4_TUNE_CACHE:-/user_4813494d/openbmb/demo-sala/assets/mm_fp4_tune_sm120.json}" \
CUTE_DSL_ARCH="${CUTE_DSL_ARCH:-sm_120a}" \
CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR="${CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR:-/user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/b12x/cache/cute_dsl}" \
SGLANG_ENABLE_B12X="${SGLANG_ENABLE_B12X:-1}" \
SGLANG_B12X_DISPATCH_PROFILE="${SGLANG_B12X_DISPATCH_PROFILE:-tuned}" \
SGLANG_B12X_PRECOMPILE="${SGLANG_B12X_PRECOMPILE:-1}" \
SGLANG_B12X_PRECOMPILE_PROFILE="${SGLANG_B12X_PRECOMPILE_PROFILE:-nospec-mini}" \
SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=0 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path "${TARGET_MODEL}" \
    --trust-remote-code --port "${PORT}" \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --max-running-requests 64 \
    --attention-backend minicpm_flashinfer \
    --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --disable-radix-cache \
    --skip-server-warmup \
    --dense-as-sparse \
    --quantization modelopt_fp4
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# =============================================================
# mini_bench.sh — 快速速度验证
#
# 用法:
#   bash bench/mini_bench.sh [API_BASE] [N_S1] [N_S8] [N_SMAX]
#
# 默认值:
#   API_BASE = http://127.0.0.1:30000
#   N_S1=8  N_S8=24  N_SMAX=64
#
# S8=24 覆盖三个满批，能体现并发压力；Smax=64 覆盖长尾。
# 数据集嵌套关系: S1(8) ⊆ S8(24) ⊆ Smax(64)，每档样本唯一。
# 本脚本取各档前 N 条，保留与全量相同的长尾特性。
# =============================================================

API_BASE="${1:-http://127.0.0.1:30000}"
N_S1="${2:-0}"
N_S8="${3:-36}"
N_SMAX="${4:-96}"

BENCH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
DATA_DIR="${BENCH_DIR}/data_full"
TOOLKIT_BENCH="${BENCH_DIR}/../toolkit/bench_serving.sh"

echo "=========================================================="
echo "  mini_bench  S1=${N_S1}  S8=${N_S8}  Smax=${N_SMAX}"
echo "  API: ${API_BASE}"
echo "=========================================================="

# 分层抽样到 /tmp（按 prompt_tokens 分布均匀取样，避免前段全是短请求）
S1_MINI="/tmp/mini_s1.jsonl"
S8_MINI="/tmp/mini_s8.jsonl"
SMAX_MINI="/tmp/mini_smax.jsonl"

python3 - <<PY
import json, random

SEED = 42
```

更小步的可行方向：
- **K1 mask** 跳 tile（已有 `_infllmv2_attn_stage1_k1_mask` 接口）：用 K2 first
  pass 输出的 evidence 限制 K1 second pass 只算选中的 K1 tiles。
- **hdim16_reduce writeout 优化**：K1 second pass 内每 tile 写 P 是必经步骤，
  看 store pattern 是否能用 `cp.async.bulk` 或减少 sync。
- **K1 second pass prologue 隐藏**：tKgK→tKsK cp.async 跟 mma_qk 并行度。


## 2026-05-17 — K1 mask ceiling vs K2-evidence reality

### K1 mask 速度 scaling (ideal)

用 `_infllmv2_attn_stage1_k1_mask` 接口，构造均匀 keep ratio 的 mask，测 stage1
时间线性度（L9 capture, max_q=8087, max_k1=32760）：

| keep_ratio | total ms | K1 second pass ms |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.0 | `41.05` | `31.5` |
| 0.75 | `33.17` | `23.6` |
| 0.5 | `25.14` | `15.6` |
| 0.25 | `17.01` | `7.4` |
| 0.125 | `12.96` | `3.4` |
| 0.0625 | `10.93` | `1.4` |

K1 second pass 时间随 keep_ratio 严格线性。这给出 K1 mask 路径的速度
**ceiling**：如果用 ideal mask（基于 exact_topk_idx 反推 K1 tile），stage1 可
以从 `41.34ms` → `~11ms`，**节省约 30ms/layer**。

### K2-evidence 实际 recall + 时间

用 Q@K2 计算 prob_groupmax_sum(radius=0), 按 K1 tile 聚合，top-M 选 K1 tile，
用 stage1_k1_mask 跑 masked K1 second pass：

| top_M K1 tiles | keep ratio | masked stage1 ms | recall vs base topk |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 320 | 62.5% | `29.08` | `98.30%` |
| 256 | 50% | `25.01` | `95.95%` |
| 192 | 37.5% | `20.96` | `90.92%` |
| 128 | 25% | `16.92` | `80.99%` |
| 96 | 18.75% | `14.90` | `72.03%` |
| 64 | 12.5% | `12.89` | `58.26%` |
| 48 | 9.4% | `11.88` | `50.20%` |
| 32 | 6.25% | `10.87` | `41.63%` |

### 负结论

- 即使 keep top-M=320（98.3% recall），masked K1 stage1 自己已经 `29ms`，节省
  `12.3ms/layer`。
- 但 K2 evidence 提取需要：K2 first pass `9.56ms` + writeout K2 prob 估 `2.1ms`
  + fast CUDA mask builder ~`4ms` + max_pool + topk `2.7ms`。
- 端到端 (K2 first pass + writeout + mask + masked K1 + pool + topk) ≈
  `9.56 + 2.1 + 4 + 29 + 2.7 = 47.4 ms` vs baseline 43.4ms（stage1+pool+topk）。
- **净亏 4 ms/layer**。

Recall 96-98% 也会影响 e2e accuracy（约 2-5% sparse block selection drift），
即使时间略平也有 accuracy 风险。

### 启示

- K1 mask 路径的关键瓶颈是 K2 evidence 的精度上限：top-M=320（62.5%）才
  达 98.3% recall，而要净赢必须 keep < 25%（~80% recall），不可接受。
- 单 K2 first pass evidence 跟 exact_topk_idx 之间存在 fundamental gap，因为
  K2 是 K1 的下采样近似。
- 后续方向应转向其它 prefill 大头（stage2 sparse FA、long-context dense layer
  等），不再寄望 K1 mask shortcut。

### Reproducer

```bash
python3 /tmp/bench_k1_mask_scaling.py    # keep_ratio 线性度
python3 /tmp/bench_k1_mask_ideal3.py     # ideal mask ceiling
python3 /tmp/bench_k2_evidence_mask.py   # K2 evidence + 时间分解
```

508	        page_id = token * 2 + head_group.  For 64-token sparse blocks, this

69	    except RuntimeError:

73	def _profile_begin() -> float:
74	    if _profile_can_sync():
75	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
76	    return time.perf_counter()
77	
78	
79	def _profile_end(start: float, bucket: str):
80	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
81	        return
82	    if _profile_can_sync():
83	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
84	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS[bucket] = _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) + (
85	        time.perf_counter() - start
86	    ) * 1000.0
87	
88	
89	def _profile_step(counter: str, buckets: tuple[str, ...], label: str):
90	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
91	        return
92	    count = _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS.get(counter, 0) + 1
93	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS[counter] = count
94	    if count % _MINICPM_PROFILE_INTERVAL != 0:
95	        return
96	    stats = ", ".join(
97	        f"{bucket}={_MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) / count:.3f}ms"
98	        for bucket in buckets
99	    )

entry\"\n- 每个 entry：`q_len=1, q_heads=16, kv_heads=1, head_dim=128`\n- 每个 entry 自己的 sparse page list（kv_indptr/kv_indices 来自\n  `triton_topk_to_flashinfer_indices`）\n- topk = 64 sparse blocks × 64 1)\n        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)\n        positions = rng.choice(qt - 1, size=sample_pairs, replace=False)\n        j_adj = [jaccard(idxs[p], idxs[p+1]) for p in positions]\n\n        # Jaccard between same-position pairs across N steps apart\n        results = {}\n        for stride in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]:\n            if qt > stride:\n                positions = rng.choice(qt - stride, size=min(500, qt-stride), replace=False)\n                js = [jaccard(idxs[p], idxs[p+stride]) for p in positions]\n                results[stride] = np.mean(js)\n\n        # Union size of windows\n        union_results = {}\n        for stride in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]:\n            if qt >= stride:\n                positions = rng.choice(qt - stride + 1, size=min(200, qt-stride+1), replace=False)\n                u = [union_size(idxs, p, stride) for p in positions]\n                union_results[stride] = (np.mean(u), tk)\n\n        print(f\"  head_group={head_group}\")\n        print(f\"    Jaccard adjacent: mean={np.mean(j_adj):.3f} median={np.median(j_adj):.3f}\")\n        print(f\"    Jaccard by stride: \" + \", \".join(f\"d={s}:{j:.3f}\" for s,j in results.items()))\n        print(f\"    Union of stride-window blocks / topk: \" +\n              \", \".join(f\"d={s}:{u:.1f}/{tk}={u/tk:.2f}x\" for s,(u,tk) in union_results.items()))\n"
}

0.55 | 2.41x | 3.24x | 4.71x |\n\n平均：adjacent Jaccard ≈ 0.52，stride=16 union ≈ 3.3× topk。\n\n### 解读\n\n- **相邻 query token 共享约 50% 的 sparse block**——L2 cache reuse 解释了\n  实测 9.74ms 比理论纯 HBM bandwidth (≈ 60ms) 快 6×。\n- **stride=16 union ≈ 3.3× topk**：把 16 个相邻 query 打包成一个 chunk，唯一\n  KV block 数 = 3.3 × 96 = 317（vs 16 × 96 = 1536 顺序读）。HBM 读量降到 1/5。\n\n### 是否有收益？粗算\n\n- 顺序 decode：16384 entries × 96 block × 16 KB = 24 GB HBM 读 / chunk\n  （考虑 L2 ~6× reuse，实测 ~9.74ms）\n- 打包 stride=16 prefill：1024 chunks × 317 block × 16 KB = 5 GB HBM 读\n  / chunk\n- 理论 HBM 节省 ~5×，但 prefill 需要算 16 × 317 × 64 = 324K K-token attention\n  per chunk × 1024 chunks ≈ 332M op (vs 顺序的 16 × 96 × 64 = 98K op/query ×\n  16384 query = 1.6G op)。所以 compute 实际**减少 5×**（不是增加），因为单\n  query 之前要算自己的全部 topk × 16 q-head，打包能去重。\n\n等等不对。打包后每个 query 必须只 attend 它自己原本选的 K 集合，否则结果错\n误。这要么需要 per-query mask（增加 mask 处理 cost），要么需要软重新算（不\n等价）。\n\n### 实施路径分支\n\nA. **Exact 等价**：FlashInfer prefill + per-query custom_mask，理论收益\n~30-50%。难点是 mask 构造和 FlashInfer prefill 支持 mask 的形状要研究清楚。\n\nB. **近似**：query 打包后 attend union of topk，不带 mask。语义是 chunk-level\ntop-K，每个 query 看到比原本多 ~3× 的 K block。精度影响未知，需 e2e 验证。\n\nC. **驳回**：直接重写 FlashInfer decode kernel 的 block schedule，按 K block\noverlap 排队 SM，降低 L2 miss 率。需要改 FlashInfer 源码或写自定义 kernel。\n\n### 优先级判断\n\n- 当前 stage2 = 9.74ms × 512 calls = 5s / 长 prefill 请求；30% 节省 = 1.5s。\n- 但实施 A/B/C 都是大工程：需要新 kernel/wrapper、accuracy 验证、调试。\n- **Stage1 的 K1 mask 路线已经验证净亏 → 别再投入 stage1 优化**。\n- 还应该看 MLP / FC / GLA prefill 占比再判断是否值得搞 stage2。\n\n### #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /user_4813494d/openbmb

# Ensure the project venv is active (scripts must not depend on caller's shell).
SALA_VENV="/opt/SGLang-MiniCPM-SALA/sglang_minicpm_sala_env"
if [[ "${VIRTUAL_ENV:-}" != "${SALA_VENV}" || "$(command -v python3)" != "${SALA_VENV}/bin/python3" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "${SALA_VENV}/bin/activate"
fi

# EAGLE-3 speculative decoding server (current production config)
# - spec_steps=3, topk=2, dtn=7  (chain verify, default D5 mode)
# - dynamic spec mode: NO_SPEC bs>=32, D7 bs<=1, D5 otherwise (theta 0.85/0.5)
# - ngram route: hit -> chain verify branch, miss -> EAGLE draft, both under cuda graph
# - target: NVFP4 (GPTQ + FourOverSix), hybrid Marlin/CUTLASS decode
# - draft:  det_prefill NVFP4 QAT, b12x explicitly off by default
#
# 只显式设置与 code 默认不同的 env；其余使用 code 默认值（参见
# sglang/srt/{environ.py,speculative/spec_mode.py,layers/.../*}）。
# 用户可在调用前 export 任一 SGLANG_*/EAGLE_* env 来覆盖。

SPEC_STEPS="${EAGLE_SPEC_STEPS:-3}"
TOPK="${EAGLE_TOPK:-2}"
# dtn = 1 + topk * spec_steps (tree nodes)
DTN=$((1 + TOPK * SPEC_STEPS))
TARGET_MODEL="${EAGLE_TARGET_MODEL:-/user_4813494d/models/openbmb/MiniCPM-SALA-gptq46-calib90-90k-NVFP4-det}"
DRAFT_MODEL="${EAGLE_DRAFT_MODEL:-/user_4813494d/openbmb/demo-sala/data/eagle_draft}"
MARS_THETA="${EAGLE_MARS_THETA:-1}"
D5_MARS_THETA="${EAGLE_D5_MARS_THETA:-0.85}"
D7_MARS_THETA="${EAGLE_D7_MARS_THETA:-0.5}"
RANDOM_SEED_ARGS=()
if [[ -n "${SGLANG_RANDOM_SEED:-}" ]]; then
    RANDOM_SEED_ARGS=(--random-seed "${SGLANG_RANDOM_SEED}")
fi

echo "[start_eagle] MARS global=${MARS_THETA} D5=${D5_MARS_THETA} D7=${D7_MARS_THETA}"

SGLANG_FP4_TUNE_CACHE="${SGLANG_FP4_TUNE_CACHE:-/user_4813494d/openbmb/demo-sala/assets/mm_fp4_tune_sm120.json}" \
SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD="${SGLANG_MARLIN_DECODE_THRESHOLD:-48}" \
CUTE_DSL_ARCH="${CUTE_DSL_ARCH:-sm_120a}" \
CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR="${CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR:-/user_4813494d/openbmb/demo-sala/assets/b12x_aot_cache}" \
SGLANG_ENABLE_B12X="${SGLANG_ENABLE_B12X:-0}" \
SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSED_GLA_QK_NORM_ROPE_OOP="${SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSED_GLA_QK_NORM_ROPE_OOP:-1}" \
SGLANG_MINICPM_GLA_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIGMOID_MUL="${SGLANG_MINICPM_GLA_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIGMOID_MUL:-1}" \
EAGLE_MARS_THETA="${MARS_THETA}" \
EAGLE_D5_MARS_THETA="${D5_MARS_THETA}" \
EAGLE_D7_MARS_THETA="${D7_MARS_THETA}" \
EAGLE_DYNAMIC_MODE="${EAGLE_DYNAMIC_MODE:-1}" \
EAGLE_NO_SPEC_BS="${EAGLE_NO_SPEC_BS:-32}" \
EAGLE_NO_SPEC_LEAVE_BS="${EAGLE_NO_SPEC_LEAVE_BS:-28}" \

# sm_120 GEMM 当前事实
> **2026-05-10 R-b12x lock-in (commit 679017f)**：production decode 已切换到 b12x (CuTe DSL W4A4 NVFP4 GEMM) target dispatch，default `SGLANG_ENABLE_B12X=1`。Decode single +28.5%、bs=8/12/16/24 +7-12%。详见 [changelog.md Round R-b12x](changelog.md)。dead-ends.md §M 旧"精度损失"判定已平反。
> **2026-05-10 R-b12x-acc-fix lock-in**：`marlin_upper` 全部抬到 48（每 shape，旧 lock-in 是 8/16/24/32）。M ≤ 48 全走 W4A16 Marlin（高精度，short-decode 路径），M > 48 保留 b12x (W4A4) 吞吐。`run_public_eval_full` 实测 ori_acc 78.64→**80.33%** (+1.69pp，cwe +6.7pp / qa +6.7pp / fwe +1.1pp)、overall_acc 98.31→**100%**；`quick_validate` 吞吐全档持平或 +0~9%（**双赢**）。
> **2026-05-10 R-marlin-fp32reduce REJECTED**：试 `SGLANG_MARLIN_USE_FP32_REDUCE=0`（marlin split-K BF16 reduce 替 FP32）。decode_single +41.5% 但 bs=8/12 -8~-10%，full eval ori_acc 80.33→**80.07%** (-0.27pp)、production duration ~同。production EAGLE-3 dtn=7 把 m 放大 8x，decode_single 收益不存在对应的工作负载；marlin M 直方图 89% 命中 M=11/32 回归区。env switch 代码保留，**default=1 不变**。详见 [changelog.md Round R-marlin-fp32reduce](changelog.md)。
> **2026-05-10 R-b12x-bucket64 REJECTED**：试加 `_M_BUCKETS = 64` + 4 个新 BEST_TILE entries（std_o/std_qkv/gla_qkv/gate_up bucket=64 explicit tile）。bench 微基显示 M=49/64 -14~-44% kernel 时间，quick_validate bs=8 +1.98% 可复现。但 full eval **ori_acc 80.33→79.27% (-1.06pp)、duration 1303→1416s (+8.7%)** 双重退化；长尾 mcq 单 batch 卡 4 分钟。教训：**新增 bucket boundary 必须 full eval gate**，quick_validate 的稳态 5-prompt 合成负载无法捕捉 production EAGLE-3 异质长输出下 dispatch 在 bucket 边界来回切换的代价。完全回退（4 entries 删除 + `_M_BUCKETS` 还原 + `_NO_SPEC_PRECOMPILE_BUCKETS` 还原）。AOT cache `M64_*.o` 文件保留 dormant。详见 [changelog.md Round R-b12x-bucket64](changelog.md)。
## 2. sm_120 NVFP4 GEMM Kernel 资源分析
| max warps/SM (sm_120) | 待 `cudaDeviceGetAttribute` 实测 | 早期文档写 48 但 C 路引用源给 64，矛盾——实测才能定 |
| Register file/SM | 64K × 32-bit = 256 KB | NVIDIA Compute Capability docs |
| max blocks/SM | 32 | — |
| SMEM/SM | 128 KB | per-SM 上限 |
**REG=168 是 NVFP4 GEMM 物理下限，不是工程师选择**：warp tile 64×64 fp32 accum = 128 reg/thread 仅 accum；+A/B frag double buffer +scale frag +addresses ≈ 168。要降 REG 必须缩 warp tile 64→32 → 复用降一半 → 得不偿失。详见 [methodology.md](methodology.md) §11 反模式 + [dead-ends.md](dead-ends.md) §B。
### 2.2 .so 内 sm_120 dense NVFP4 GEMM 实例
| **Cooperative** (`KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperativeBlockScaledSm120`) | 4 | 168 | 1024 | 0 / 8 | **dense GEMM 主用** |
| **PingpongBlockScaled** (`KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecializedPingpongBlockScaledSm120`) | 1 | 168 | 1024 | 16 | grouped GEMM (我们不用 MoE) |
Marlin 在 sm_120 上 reg 100-127，比 NVFP4 dense GEMM 168 低（W4A16 算法侧 reg 需求小）—— 这是 Marlin 在小 M (decode) 优于 CUTLASS NVFP4 的硬件层物理依据之一（[methodology.md](methodology.md) §3 M regime）。
| `Sm100*` (tcgen05 / UMMA) | 52 | sm_120 没有 tcgen05 / TMEM |
`demo-sala/sglang/.../marlin_utils_fp4.py` 与上游 `sgl-project/sglang PR #19652` 的差异是 cosmetic（import 路径、注释中文化、删除 `direct_register_custom_op`）。**`nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` 算法完全相同**，没有 vLLM PR #34577 等价 fix。
**只做了简单 right-shift 4，没做 exponent rebias**（FP8-S0E5M3 bias=15 vs BF16 bias=127）。与 vLLM PR #34577 报告的 BF16 widening underflow bug 形态一致：small global_scale 路径 → `2^-112` underflow。生产路径走 BF16 activation，**这个 bug 是相关的**，但当前未实测确认。
- **升 CUTLASS 4.4.2 对 sm_120 dense GEMM 性能几乎无影响**（kernel 代码 ≡ 4.2.0）
- 唯一稳定收益：**`alignas(16)` SMEM scale alignment fix**（修潜在 corruption），可直接 cherry-pick 不需要全升级
- **max warps/SM = 48**（2026-05-10 `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(cudaDevAttrMaxThreadsPerMultiProcessor)=1536`，156 SM，max blocks/SM=24，max regs/SM=65536，max SMEM/SM=102400 = 100 KB；与 [hardware.md](hardware.md) §1 一致；C 路报告 max warps=64 是 sm_100 数字，**不适用 sm_120**）
- **`.so` 实际 spill 量**：[changelog.md R1.3](changelog.md) 已实证（同一 md5 `c22699c...` .so）：cubin #39 = 67 生产 marlin kernel，1128 LDL/STL = avg 17/kernel；最高 47 在 `TileM=128 stages=4 TN=4 TK=8`。spill 17 条 vs HMMA 几千条 = ~0.5% cycle 占比，**不是 SOL 18% 主因**。stages=4 + 中等 tile 是 spill 高发组合，但量级不致命

# Prefill Research Roadmap

This roadmap is for main-test prefill only.

Current stage1 groupmax kernel design note:
`prefill/stage1-groupmax-design.md`.

## Working Bottleneck Model

At `chunked-prefill-size=8192`, a 128K-ish request has around 16 chunks. A 524K-ish request has around 64 chunks. This changes the priority order.

Approximate cost model:

| Component | 128K / 16 chunks | 524K / 64 chunks | Scaling |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| MLP FP4 GEMM path | ~2.1s | ~8.5s | linear in chunks |
| GLA path | ~1.5s | ~6.1s | linear in chunks |
| sparse stage2 | ~1.3s | ~5.4s | linear in chunks |
| sparse stage1 | ~0.7s | ~10.8s | grows with context/history |

The most important update is sparse stage1: it can be modest at 128K and dominant at 524K.

## P0: Confirm Actual Main-Test Surface

Goal: profile accepted requests under official benchmark behavior, not hypothetical rows that length rules filter out.

Experiments:

1. Run the official wrapper on `bench/data_full` and record final `S1/S8/Smax` durations.
2. Capture the number of rows sampled by `sglang.bench_serving` after pruning.
3. Record length-related errors separately from non-length runtime failures.
4. Profile one accepted ~128K request and one accepted ~500K request.

This is not an attempt to bypass length filtering. It is just making the measured surface explicit.

## P0: MLP Gated FP4 Epilogue

Current MLP path:

```text
fp4 gate_up GEMM -> BF16 gate_up [M, 2*inter]
BF16 gate_up -> silu(gate) * up + FP4 quant
FP4 activation -> fp4 down GEMM
```

The expensive part is not only the activation kernel. The larger waste is writing and rereading the BF16 gate/up intermediate. For full chunks this intermediate is roughly:

```text
8192 * 32768 * 2 bytes = 512 MiB
```

Research target:

- Implement an SM120 dense-only `gate_up_swiglu_fp4` epilogue.
- Consume paired gate/up accumulators directly.
- Compute `silu(gate) * up` in the epilogue.
- Emit the FP4 activation and block scales directly in the layout expected by the current down projection.

Proof bar:

- Synthetic downstream diff against current BF16-intermediate path.
- Real prompt output sanity.
- Public accuracy guard if numerical differences are non-bitwise.
- End-to-end benchmark gain on accepted main-test rows.

Rejected nearby paths:

- Dense-as-MoE wrapper: numerically feasible but only about 1% full-chunk layer speedup and high integration risk.
- Quantizing gate/up to FP4 before SwiGLU: slower and numerically much worse.
- Broad cuDNN MLP switching: tail-shape numerical risk and no stable e2e win.

Latest backend recheck:

- Full-chunk cuDNN FP4 GEMM is only about `1.014x` faster for gate_up and
  `1.050x` faster for down than CUTLASS on the current RTX 6000D environment.
- Tail-shape cuDNN GEMM is faster, but numerical drift is large
  (`max_diff` about `3.7-3.9`), so it is not a safe backend switch.
- cuDNN `gemm_swiglu` FP4 fails to compile on current `sm_120`
  (`expects arch ... sm_100a/sm_103a, got sm_120a`).
- Therefore the remaining MLP opportunity is still a custom fused epilogue that

395 /user_4813494d/openbmb/prefill/roadmap.md
- Therefore the remaining MLP opportunity is still a custom fused epilogue that
  avoids the BF16 gate/up intermediate; no low-risk backend flag is available.

Latest production-path A/B:

- `SGLANG_MINICPM_FUSED_MLP_ACT_QUANT=1` is a real e2e win on line91.
- No-profile line91 steady avg: fused ON `34.818s`, fused OFF `35.284s`.
- Gain: about `0.465s`, or `1.32%` wall-time.
- This path is already default ON and is reachable for the target model because
  `pre_quant_scale=false`; it should be preserved, but it is not additional
  remaining headroom.

## P0: Exact Sparse Stage1 Fusion

Current stage1 work computes score/pool/topk for sparse block selection. Existing trait tuning is mostly exhausted; at 524K the context/history scaling makes this path a leading target.

Latest offline profile on the longest accepted line91 shape:

- Tail shape: `seq_len=524183`, `q_len=8087`, `score=[2, 8087, 32768]`
- Stage1 alone: `40.6ms/layer`, about `325ms/chunk` across 8 sparse layers
- Full `stage1 -> pool -> topk`: `43.1ms/layer`, about `345ms/chunk`
- Torch profiler: `flash_fwd_splitkv_stage1_kernel` is about `92%` of CUDA time
- Manual offline topk matches production `compressed_attention` topk on the sweeped shapes

Research target:

- Fuse exact `score -> pool -> topk` where semantics allow.
- Avoid materializing large intermediate score tensors.
- Preserve current K1+K2 semantics, causal/pool boundaries, topk order, and selected blocks.

Proof bar:

- Use `prefill/stage1_offline_profile.py` as the first exact topk oracle.
- Topk indices identical on production shapes and tail shapes.
- Hidden/logit or answer checks on long-context examples.
- Profile shows stage1 bucket reduction on 524K-scale accepted requests.

Secondary small target:

- InfLLM-v2 empty-P2 prototype: replace the full score output fill with empty allocation plus a targeted future/padding zero kernel. This is exact for the tested direct-pool production shapes and gives the line91 single-request run about `0.53%` steady-state gain. It remains default-off until mixed-batch and public-set checks pass.

Practical read:

- The empty-P2 work is a good small candidate for later packaging.
- It does not change the bottleneck: late stage1 still spends about `40ms/layer` in `flash_fwd_splitkv_stage1_kernel`.
- Further meaningful prefill gain needs to reduce the core stage1 work or avoid materializing the `[2, q_len, rounded_k1_len]` score tensor.

Updated upper-bound read:

- Removing P writes alone only moves line91 full stage1 from about `10.68s` to `10.43s`.
- Exact stage1-to-blockmax/topk fusion can also remove pool/topk, but the line91 ceiling is still only about `1.0s`.
- Returning after the first stage1 pass would reduce the line91 stage1 bucket to about `2.17s`, exposing a `~9.26s` upper bound.

Therefore exact fusion is no longer the highest-upside option. It remains the
safe fallback, while the high-upside research path is candidate selection from
K2/low-resolution evidence plus selective K1 refinement.

Latest exact-fusion implementation read:

- The first in-stage1 blockmax prototype was exact but slow: about `188.8ms`
  versus `43ms` for the old `stage1 -> max_pool -> topk` path on L9.
- Rewriting pooling from atomics to a shared 64-score tile made it exact and
  much faster, but still negative: shared-score stage1 blockmax is about
  `51.4ms`, and blockmax + topk is about `52.9ms`.
- The old path on the same capture is about `40.7ms` stage1, `1.2ms` pool, and
  `1.5ms` topk. Therefore exact blockmax inside the current stage1 loop is not
  a packaging candidate; it remains only a correctness oracle.

## P0: K2 Candidate Selection Plus K1 Refinement

Goal: avoid the full second K1 scan in stage1.

Current stage1 has two large pieces:

```text
first pass:  K2/coarse denominator pass
second pass: K1 normalized per-column score pass -> pool -> topk
```

The first pass is about `2.17s` across the line91 request, while full stage1 is
about `10.68s`. This creates the only visible multi-second opportunity.

Candidate design:

1. Use K2/coarse scores to select a wider candidate set of blocks.
2. Expand candidates to neighboring K1 blocks to cover pooling overlap and
   boundary effects.
3. Run exact K1 scoring only for that candidate set.
4. Keep the existing stage2 attention semantics unchanged.

Proof bar:

- Offline candidate recall against current exact topk on real hidden states, not synthetic random tensors.
- Report recall@topk for multipliers such as `2x`, `4x`, `8x`.
- Public accuracy and long-context sanity before any speed result matters.
- If recall is not high enough, do not use this path as a submission optimization.

Hard non-goal:

- Do not shrink candidates/topk or drop K2 unless an offline proof shows exact equivalence. Approximate block selection is an accuracy research project, not a submission-speed shortcut.

Latest line91 capture result:

- Captured real tail tensors for 8 sparse layers: `0, 9, 16, 17, 22, 29, 30, 31`.
- K2 mapping must treat coarse token `c` as covering sparse blocks `{c, c+1}`
  before neighbor expansion.
- Corrected multi-topk sweep uses score-sorted K2 indices before slicing smaller
  top-k values.
- For the implemented K1 tile mask, tile recall is the relevant metric.
- K2 `topk=1024,radius=8` after layer 0 has tile recall about
  `99.77-99.96%` and candidate tile fraction about `52.5-59.7%`.
- Layer 0 is still the outlier: `topk=1024,radius=8` tile recall is only about
  `98.23%`, and candidate tile fraction is already about `81.1%`.
- K2 `topk=1536,radius=8` improves later-layer tile recall to roughly
  `99.92-99.99%`, but candidate tile fraction rises to about `62.6-70.8%`.
- Best current design is therefore layer-specific: keep layer 0 exact, use K2
  selective refinement on later sparse layers, and keep an exact fallback/check
  gate. This is still approximate until full answer/accuracy checks pass.

```
- InfLLM stage1 already has a `fwdIterator` blockmask path in
  `kernels/infllmv2_cuda_impl/csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_blockmask.h`.
- Current `mha_varlen_fwd_stage1` does not expose a second-pass-only candidate
  mask. Passing the existing `params.blockmask` directly would also affect the
  first K2 denominator pass, which is semantically wrong.
- Minimal prototype already added a separate stage1 K1-pass mask pointer for
  offline tests. With the mask supplied for free, later-layer masked stage1 drops
  from about `39.4ms` to about `24-27ms` at `topk=1024,radius=8`, or to about
  `28-31ms` at `topk=1536,radius=8`.
- The two-call online prototype is not viable because K2 score + mask build adds
  about `20-21ms/layer`, making total time slower than full stage1.
- The next real kernel cut must generate a K2-probability-derived tile candidate
  inside stage1 after K2 denominator information is available, then feed the
  existing second-pass K1 mask iterator. Raw K2 logits and simple score-threshold
  candidates were rejected: they either lose recall or retain nearly all tiles.
- A more implementable variant is K2 tile-score top-M:
  - reduce K2 probability evidence into `512` K1 tile scores,
  - expand by radius before tile scoring,
  - keep fixed top-M tiles instead of doing topk over about `8192` K2 tokens.
- On L9, top-M `320` gives about `99.78%` tile recall and `28.6ms` masked
  stage1; top-M `384` gives about `99.92%` tile recall and `32.8ms` masked
  stage1. Full stage1 is about `39.4ms`.
- Across later layers, top-M `320` is about `99.78-99.97%` tile recall, while
  top-M `384` is about `99.88-99.99%`. Layer 0 remains exact-only.
- The Python validation harness takes about `284ms` just to build L9 tile
  scores, so it is not an online path. It is only a correctness/speed-bound
  oracle for an in-stage1 implementation.
- Later-layer masked stage1 time is stable. Including `tile_score -> top-M mask`
  construction from precomputed tile scores, top-M `320` is about
  `29.44ms/layer`, top-M `352` about `31.42ms/layer`, and top-M `384` about
  `33.55ms/layer`.
- Mask construction is only about `0.40ms/layer`, so top-M/mask formation is not
  the bottleneck once normalized tile scores exist.
- With layer 0 exact, the tail-stage bound is roughly `77.7ms/chunk` saved for
  top-M `320`, `63.9ms/chunk` for top-M `352`, and `49.0ms/chunk` for top-M
  `384`.
- A design that needs another K2 scan after denominator finalization is probably
  too weak: subtracting about `8.4ms/layer` leaves only about `16ms/chunk` tail
  gain for top-M `320` before selection overhead, and makes top-M `384`
  unattractive.
- Therefore the only worthwhile tile-score kernel variant must maintain useful
  denominator-aware tile evidence during the existing K2 pass. If that cannot be
  made accurate enough, move attention to another prefill bottleneck rather than
  building a second-K2-pass stage1.
- Across later layers, normalized `prob_sum` is still the quality leader:
  top-M `384` mean recall `99.978%`, min recall `99.921%`. Denominator-free
  `exp_sum` top-M `384` is weaker but not hopeless: mean `99.936%`, min
  `99.803%`. Raw-logit max is rejected: top-M `384` mean recall is only
  `96.508%`.
- Tile-mass evidence is easier to imagine as an online accumulator, but it is
  not the best high-yield point. `prob_tile_sum` needs top-M `416` to reach
  mean recall `99.975%`, min recall `99.918%`, and that candidate width cuts the
  7-layer tail bound to only about `34.3ms/chunk` saved.
- Best current implementation-facing variant: `prob_groupmax_sum`. It keeps a
  per-query-head-group tile max, then sums those group maxima. Excluding layer 0,
  top-M `320` has mean recall `99.915%`, min `99.785%`; top-M `352` has mean
  `99.956%`, min `99.870%`; top-M `384` has mean `99.978%`, min `99.915%`.
  This matches normalized `prob_sum` quality closely while giving a clearer
  online-rescale implementation shape.
- Offline online-rescale simulation with K2 block size `64` exactly matches
  `prob_groupmax_sum` on all eight captures: `0` mismatches for hits, totals,
  recall, and full-row rate. The remaining question is therefore CUDA storage
  and reduction cost, not whether the evidence can be generated without a
  second K2 scan.
- Layout check is favorable: `_adjust_stage1_q` converts `(total_q, 32, 128)`
  into `(total_q * 16, 2, 128)`, and stage1 uses `kBlockM=16`, `kBlockN=64`.
  One CTA row block is exactly the 16 query-head group rows for one original
  token and one KV head, matching the `prob_groupmax_sum` reduction.
- bf16 tile-max storage appears safe in the offline online-rescale simulation:
  top-M `384` mean/min recall is `99.978%` / `99.916%`, with per-layer hit diff
  versus fp32 online in `[-1, +6]`. This reduces extra shared memory from
  `32KB/CTA` to `16KB/CTA`, making the first CUDA prototype more realistic.
- The kernel cut should either keep candidate generation and masked K1
  refinement inside one launch, or split with explicit first-pass `row_max` /
  `row_sum` outputs. A second call that recomputes K2 is still rejected.

Rejected shortcut:

- Existing `--fuse-topk` was tried online on line91. It slowed prefill chunks
  to roughly `6-7s/chunk`, far slower than the default path, so the current
  TileLang fused-topk path is not a usable P0 shortcut.

Parallel approximate candidate:

- Head-subset candidate selection with `candidate_topk=256`:
  - `h12`: global recall mean `99.28%`, min `98.56%`.
  - `h14`: global recall mean `99.69%`, min `99.38%`.
- The recall is strong, but the speed model is weaker because `h14` still scans
  `87.5%` of query heads and would need a new stage1 kernel. Keep it behind K2
  selective refinement in priority.

## P0/P1: Exact Sparse Stage2 Kernel/Layout

Current stage2 uses FlashInfer over row-wise sparse page tables. The production shape is many query rows with top-k blocks per row. Existing page64, two-wrapper, blocksplit+merge, and simple Triton direct paths did not produce stable e2e wins.

Research target:

- Either make FlashInfer select a better low-register/specialized variant for this exact shape, or build a single exact block-sparse kernel/layout that consumes `topk_idx` directly.
- Avoid dual-wrapper and merge overhead.
- Preserve exact causal partial-block behavior.

Proof bar:

- Same selected KV blocks and same output tolerance.
- Stage2 bucket decreases under profile.
- End-to-end wall improvement survives A/B/A runs.

## P1: Chunk Size Re-Sweep Under Main Workload

`chunked-prefill-size=16384` was slower on the old line-39-style benchmark. Because `bench/data_full` includes 500K-scale rows, re-sweep only after accepted-request behavior is clear.

Candidate sweep:

```text
4096, 8192, 12288, 16384
```

Required measurements:

- Accepted row count unchanged except expected protocol filtering.
```

1	# Stage1 Groupmax Tile Candidate Design
2	
3	This note tracks the current highest-upside prefill stage1 path:
4	`prob_groupmax_sum` tile candidates generated during the existing K2 first pass.
5	
6	## Why This Candidate
7	
8	The previous normalized `prob_sum` tile score has strong recall, but exact tile
9	max over the sum of query-head probabilities is awkward to maintain online.
10	
11	`prob_groupmax_sum` changes the order:
12	
13	```text
14	for each KV head and original token:
15	  for each of 16 query-head group rows:
16	    keep max probability per K1 tile
17	  sum the 16 group tile maxima
18	  select top-M tiles
19	```
20	
21	Offline recall on the line91 tail captures, excluding layer 0:
22	
23	| Evidence | top-M | Mean recall | Min recall |
24	|---|---:|---:|---:|
25	| `prob_groupmax_sum` | `320` | `99.915%` | `99.785%` |
26	| `prob_groupmax_sum` | `352` | `99.956%` | `99.870%` |
27	| `prob_groupmax_sum` | `384` | `99.978%` | `99.915%` |
28	
29	The best implementation form is `logit_groupmax_norm`: keep the raw logit max
30	per group/tile, then normalize with the first-pass row max / row sum. This is
31	mathematically equivalent to `prob_groupmax_sum` because exp/softmax is
32	monotonic for a fixed row.
33	
34	All eight captured layers match exactly:
35	
36	| Evidence | Mismatches vs `prob_groupmax_sum` |
37	|---|---:|
38	| `logit_groupmax_norm` | `0` |
39	| `logit_groupmax_norm_bf16` | `0` |
40	
41	## Layout Fit
42	
43	Production stage1 already reshapes Q in the right way:
44	
45	```text
46	q:             (total_q, 32, 128)
47	_adjust_q:     (total_q * 16, 2, 128)
48	stage1 kernel: kBlockM=16, kBlockN=64
49	```
50	
51	One CTA row block therefore maps to:
52	
53	```text
54	one original token
55	one KV head
56	16 query-head group rows
57	```
58	
59	That is exactly the reduction unit needed by `prob_groupmax_sum`.
60	
61	## Storage Estimate
62	
63	For the line91 tail shape:
64	
65	```text
66	original rows: 8087
67	KV heads:      2
68	group rows:    16
69	num K1 tiles:  512
70	```
71	
72	Per CTA tile-max storage:
73	
74	| Tile max dtype | Extra storage | Current read |
75	|---|---:|
76	| fp32 raw logit | `32KB/CTA` | exact simulation reference |
77	| bf16 raw logit | `16KB/CTA` | exact match in offline simulation |
78	| fp16 | `16KB/CTA` | not checked yet |
79	
80	Current stage1 shared memory for `kBlockM=16,kBlockN=64,head_dim=128` is about:
81	
82	```text
83	Q smem:    4KB
84	K2 smem:  32KB
85	total:    36KB/CTA
86	```
87	
88	Adding fp32 tile max gives about `68KB/CTA`; adding bf16/fp16 gives about
89	`52KB/CTA`. The bf16 raw-logit version is now the preferred storage point; it
90	matches the fp32/probability evidence exactly in the offline check and cuts the
91	extra shared memory in half.
92	
93	Global outputs for a split implementation:
94	
95	| Output | Size |
96	|---|---:|
97	| fp32 tile scores `(2, 8087, 512)` | `31.6MiB` |
98	| bf16/fp16 tile scores | `15.8MiB` |
99	| row `max/sum` for adjusted rows | `2.0MiB` |
100	| uint64 tile mask `(2, 8087, 8)` | `0.99MiB` |
101	
102	## Implementation Options
103	
104	### Option A: One-Kernel Fused Stage1
105	
106	Keep everything inside the existing stage1 launch:
107	
108	1. During the K2 first pass, maintain per-group raw-logit tile max.
109	2. After `softmax.get_row_sum()`, normalize tile maxima and sum across the 16
110	   group rows.
111	3. Select top-M tiles and build a local 512-bit tile mask.
112	4. Run the existing second K1 pass through the local mask.
113	
114	Pros:
115	
116	- No second K2 scan.
117	- No global row-stat output.
118	- Best chance to approach the measured masked-stage1 bound.
119	
120	Risks:
121	
122	- In-kernel top-M over 512 tile scores may add nontrivial overhead.
123	- Extra shared memory may reduce occupancy.
124	- The current `fwdIterator` consumes global masks; a local-mask iterator or
125	  branch is needed.
126	
127	### Option B: Split First-Pass Evidence
128	
129	Split into multiple kernels:
130	
131	1. First pass emits tile scores and row `max/sum`.
132	2. Existing or new top-M mask kernel converts tile scores into a uint64 mask.
133	3. A second-pass-only K1 kernel consumes row `max/sum` and the K1 tile mask.
134	
135	Pros:
136	
137	- Simpler top-M/mask implementation.
138	- Easier to verify against the Python online simulation.
139	
140	Risks:
141	
142	- Requires a second-pass-only stage1 API.
143	- Writes tile scores and row stats to global memory.
144	- More launch overhead and more integration surface.
145	
146	## Current Choice
147	
148	Start with Option A unless the top-M/local-mask code becomes too invasive.
149	Option B is the fallback if we need a simpler correctness bridge.
150	
151	Use bf16 shared storage for raw-logit tile maxima first. Keep fp32 row max /
152	row sum.
153	
154	Layer policy remains:
155	
156	```text
157	L0 exact
158	L9+ prob_groupmax_sum selective
159	top-M 320 or 352 for first speed prototype
160	top-M 384 as accuracy fallback
161	```
162

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Evaluate K2 tile candidates for fused stage1 research.

This is closer to an implementable kernel plan than K2-token topk: reduce K2
evidence into 64-token K1 tiles, expand by radius, then keep top-M tiles per
row/head.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from stage1_k2_candidate_recall import forced_block_mask, parse_int_list


DEFAULT_CAPTURE_GLOB = "/tmp/prefill_stage1_capture8/stage1_candidate_*.pt"


def resolve_captures(pattern: str) -> list[Path]:
    paths = [Path(path) for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern))]
    if not paths:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no capture files matched {pattern!r}")
    return paths


def update_stats(stats: dict[str, int], *, hit: torch.Tensor, total: torch.Tensor, count: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    valid_rows = total > 0
    stats["hit"] += int(hit.sum().item())
    stats["total"] += int(total.sum().item())
    stats["full_rows"] += int(((hit == total) & valid_rows).sum().item())
    stats["rows"] += int(valid_rows.sum().item())
    stats["candidate_sum"] += int(count[valid_rows].sum().item())
    stats["candidate_max"] = max(stats["candidate_max"], int(count.max().item()))


def run_capture(path: Path, args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[dict[str, float | int | str]]:
    data = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu")
    device = torch.device(args.device)
    q_cpu = data["query_layer"]
    k2_cpu = data["compressed_k2"]
    exact_cpu = data["exact_topk_idx"]

    block_size = int(data["block_size"])
    init_blocks = int(data["init_blocks"])

> AGENT

This turn produced these concrete findings:

1. **stage2 sparse FA architecture** — discovered it runs as FlashInfer **decode** wrapper (not prefill) over 16K batch entries per chunk, because `sparse_max_seq_len_q=1` makes `is_prefill=False`. The 9.74ms/call cost is dominated by L2-amplified HBM traffic, not compute.

2. **Full 524K prefill breakdown** validated at 53.14s wall:
   - Stage1 ≈ 10s (18%) — explored, K1-mask path net negative
   - Stage2 ≈ 7s (13%) — needs query batching + custom mask
   - MLP ≈ 9.5s (17%) — needs gated FP4 epilogue (custom CUDA)
   - GLA ≈ 7s (13%) — bounded at 3-5× FP4 peak
   - Other ≈ 20s (39%)

3. **chunk_size dead axis** — 4096 vs 8192 within 0.1% (53.19s vs 53.14s). Corrected math: stage1 total work = total² / 2, independent of chunk_size.

4. **K2-evidence recall validated** with proper `radius=8` + `prob_groupmax_sum`:
   - L0: 97% even at top-M=384 — must keep exact
   - L9-L31 tail layers: ≥99.79% at top-M=320 — production-grade
   - Earlier 98.30% negative result was due to radius=0 + wrong mapping

5. **In-kernel groupmax is the #1 remaining concrete optimization** (Task #17): predicted 0.5-5s wall savings (0.9-9% e2e). Design in `prefill/stage1-groupmax-design.md`; the implementation requires CUDA work in `flash_fwd_kernel.h` to maintain bf16 group-tile-max in 16KB/CTA SMEM during K2 first pass, then in-kernel top-M and mask consumption in K1 second pass.

All findings written to `prefill/experiment-log.md`. Task #17 captures the next implementation step.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Discovered stage2 architecture**: Sparse prefill goes through FlashInfer **decode wrapper** (not prefill wrapper) because `sparse_max_seq_len_q=1` makes `is_prefill=False` in `FlashInferKernel.forward`. 16K decode batch entries per chunk, kept fast by L2 cache reuse (~6× amplification over raw HBM).
   - **Killed chunk_size optimization**: Validated via 3-run avg that 4096 (53.19s) ≈ 8192 (53.14s); corrected math shows stage1 total work = total² / 2, independent of chunk_size.
   - **Validated K2-evidence recall ceiling**: Tail layers (L9-L31) achieve 99.79%+ recall at top_M=320 with prob_groupmax_sum + radius=8. L0 caps at 97% even at top_M=384 — must keep exact.
   - **Started in-kernel groupmax implementation**: Added C++ scaffolding (flash.h fields, flash_api.cpp env var + tensor allocation + return), but kernel implementation in `flash_fwd_kernel.h` is not yet done.

120	__forceinline__ __device__ Element u16_to_element(uint16_t bits) {

126	template <typename Element, typename E1, typename L1>
127	__forceinline__ __device__ void hdim16_reduce_blockmax(
128	    Tensor<E1, L1> &acc_S,
129	    Element *g_blockmax,
130	    const int out_stride,
131	    const int col_idx_offset_,
132	    const int row_idx_offset_,
133	    const int warp_row_stride) {
134	
135	    auto tensor = make_tensor(acc_S.data(), flash::convert_layout_acc_rowcol(acc_S.layout()));
136	    const int lane_id = threadIdx.x % 32;
137	    const int col_idx_offset = (lane_id % 4) * 2;
138	    const int pool_base = col_idx_offset_ >> 2;
139	    (void)row_idx_offset_;
140	    (void)warp_row_stride;
141	
142	    __shared__ uint16_t score_bits[64];
143	
144	    using TensorT = decltype(make_tensor<float>(Shape< Int<size<0, 1>(tensor)>, Int<size<1>(tensor)> >{}));
145	    TensorT v02;
146	    clear(v02);
147	    #pragma unroll
148	    for (int mi = 0; mi < size<0, 1>(tensor); ++mi) {
149	        #pragma unroll
150	        for (int nj = 0; nj < size<1, 1>(tensor); ++nj) {
151	            #pragma unroll
152	            for (int j = 0; j < size<1, 0>(tensor); ++j) {
153	                const int col_idx_v02 = j * size<1, 1>(tensor) + nj;
154	                const float v0 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(0, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
155	                const float v2 = minusinf_to_zero(tensor(make_coord(1, mi), make_coord(j, nj)));
156	                v02(mi, col_idx_v02) = v0 + v2;
157	            }
158	        }
159	    }
160	
161	    SumOp<float> sum_op;
162	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<16>(v02, sum_op);
163	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<8> (v02, sum_op);
164	    thread_element_wise_reduce_<4> (v02, sum_op);
165	
166	    cutlass::NumericConverter<Element, float> converter;
167	    if (lane_id < 4) {
168	        #pragma unroll
169	        for (int mi = 0; mi < size<0, 1>(tensor); ++mi) {
170	            #pragma unroll
171	            for (int nj = 0; nj < size<1, 1>(tensor); ++nj) {
172	                const int col_idx_base = col_idx_offset + nj * 8;
173	                #pragma unroll
174	                for (int j = 0; j < size<1, 0>(tensor); ++j) {
175	                    const int col_idx = col_idx_base + j;
176	                    const int col_idx_v02 = j * size<1, 1>(tensor) + nj;
177	                    Element v = converter(v02(mi, col_idx_v02));
178	                    score_bits[col_idx] = element_to_u16(v);
179	                }
180	            }
181	        }
182	    }
183	    __syncwarp();
184	
185	    Element *row = g_blockmax;
186	    if (threadIdx.x < 17) {
187	        const int local_pool = threadIdx.x;
188	        const int pool_idx = pool_base + local_pool;
189	        if (pool_idx < out_stride) {
190	            uint16_t max_bits = 0;
191	            const int score_idx0 = local_pool * 4 - 1;
192	            if (score_idx0 >= 0) {
193	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[score_idx0]);
194	            }
195	            if (local_pool < 16) {
196	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4]);
197	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 1]);
198	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 2]);
199	                max_bits = max(max_bits, score_bits[local_pool * 4 + 3]);
200	            }
201	            if (local_pool == 0 || local_pool == 16) {
202	                const uint16_t old_bits = element_to_u16(row[pool_idx]);
203	                max_bits = max(max_bits, old_bits);
204	                row[pool_idx] = u16_to_element<Element>(max_bits);
205	            } else {
206	                row[pool_idx] = u16_to_element<Element>(max_bits);
207	            }
208	        }
209	    }
210	}

214	template<typename ElementAccum, typename Params, int kBlockM, bool Is_even_MN>
215	__forceinline__ __device__ auto get_lse_tile(const Params &params, const int bidb, const int bidh, const int m_block, const BlockInfo</*Varlen=*/!Is_even_MN> &binfo) {
216	        // When params.unpadded_lse is false, LSE is written as (b, h, seqlen_q) - this is non-variable seqlen path.
217	        // Otherwise, when params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped is true, it is written as (h, seqlen_q, b) to account for seqlen_q <-> h swapping trick.
218	        // Otherwise, it's written as (h, b, seqlen_q).
219	        const bool varlen_q = params.unpadded_lse && !params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped;
220	        auto lse_offset = varlen_q ? binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb) : 0;
221	        auto gmem_ptr_lse = make_gmem_ptr(reinterpret_cast<ElementAccum*>(params.softmax_lse_ptr) + lse_offset);
222	
223	        auto lse_shape = varlen_q ? make_shape(1, params.h, params.total_q) : make_shape(params.b, params.h, params.seqlen_q);
224	        auto lse_stride = params.seqlenq_ngroups_swapped ? make_stride(1, params.seqlen_q * params.b, params.b) : (
225	            params.unpadded_lse ? make_stride(params.h * params.total_q, params.total_q, 1) :  make_stride(params.h * params.seqlen_q, params.seqlen_q, 1)
226	            );
227	
228	        auto lse_layout = make_layout(lse_shape, lse_stride);
229	        Tensor mLSE = make_tensor(gmem_ptr_lse, lse_layout);
230	        auto mLSE_slice = varlen_q ? mLSE(0, bidh, _) : mLSE(bidb, bidh, _);
231	        return local_tile(mLSE_slice, Shape<Int<kBlockM>>{}, make_coord(m_block));
232	}

1041	## 2026-05-17 — stage1 K2 first vs K1 second 实际耗时校准

1043	### Background
1044

1048	（site-packages 安装的版本，md5=389ead90c954c2d7d06f3eb2d03eda91）不包含这段代码。

1050	整 stage1，被误读成 "K1 second pass 几乎免费"。

1080	
1081	K1 second pass + writeout 是真正的 prefill 大头：32 ms/layer × 8 sparse layers ×
1082	64 chunks ≈ 16.4 s per line91 request。理论上跳过 K1 second pass 用 K2 evidence 直
1083	接生成 candidate 能拿大头收益，但语义变更大、需要 e2e accuracy 验证。
